title: Bit shifts work on 128 bits
verdict: `BITSHIFTLEFT` keeps bits past 64; a negative count raises; refused (see #271)
description: `BITSHIFTLEFT(-8, 63)` is `-73786976294838206464` and `BITSHIFTLEFT(2^63 - 1, 63)` a 39-digit number: shifts act on 128-bit values, so bits shifted past 64 stay. From 127 on the result is 0 (or -1 shifting right a negative). A negative count raises `shift parameter must be greater or equal to zero`.
`BITAND`, `BITOR`, `BITXOR`, `BITNOT` are two's complement on the same 128 bits (`BITNOT(2^64)` is `-2^64 - 1`); their type is the input's (`NUMBER(19,0)`).
reference: `shift_left`, `shift_right` on 64 bits: bits shifted out are lost, a count outside `[0, 64)` raises (ST-1). sverify's function table refuses Snowflake's shifts (`_functions.py`, "not 64-bit").

provenance.checked_by: sverify_dev.probe_snowflake through the Snowflake CLI (Snowflake characterization session)

evidence.sql: SELECT n, bitshiftleft(a, n), bitshiftright(a, n), SYSTEM$TYPEOF(bitshiftleft(a, n)) FROM (VALUES (-8, 1), (-8, 7), (-8, 63), (-8, 64), (-8, 65), (-8, 127), (-8, 128), (-8, 129)) AS s(a, n)

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_snowflake` runs each query through `snow sql` (Snowflake CLI 3.32.1) on an X-Small warehouse, Snowflake 10.40.102, with the session's `TIMEZONE` set to UTC and `USE_CACHED_RESULT` off; every other parameter is the account's default, recorded in the header of probes.json (`WEEK_START` 0, `WEEK_OF_YEAR_POLICY` 0, `DEFAULT_NULL_ORDERING` LAST, `TIMESTAMP_TYPE_MAPPING` TIMESTAMP_NTZ). The inputs are literal `VALUES`, except the `sample-*` probes, which read TPC-H's LINEITEM (6,001,215 rows) in SNOWFLAKE_SAMPLE_DATA.
